reviewer: Claude (independent read-only review; did not author the checkpoint)
target: integrations/puredarwin/chonkstep-darwin/desktop-shell checkpoint 001: source set 4202fedc1f12b52b204bb94f88b8df299f907547e5902804a3ed590bf428b42b, shell.patch add1c06e, onto the deployed717 baseline source (runs/m1-desktop-010/keyboard-only-compositor-build-001/source)
scope_split: On root's instruction this review covers the shared Shell, the standalone profile's external side effects, the modal PopupHost, input ownership, the cascade and the overall foundation. The applications.rs, terminal_launch.rs and launch_audit.rs internals (C ABI, PID ownership, status protocol, deadlines, journal) belong to the separate desktop-shell-owned-applications-independent-review.json. Only cross-boundary observations about them appear here.
verdict: SOURCE FOUNDATION APPROVED FOR CONTINUED WORK; NOT AN ADMISSION. The real Shell, Desktop and cascade run over the CPU PopupHost. The standalone profile genuinely removes its external service owners and refuses unsupported actions. I found no external side effect reachable in standalone on the paths examined. Input ownership is modal and keeps clients consistent (leave on grab, deferred focus until all keys are released). The non-blocking notes below and the checkpoint's own admission_remaining list stand. No native entry exists (main.rs is unchanged), and no runtime, Darwin spawn, input or display claim follows.

binding.replay: verify_checkpoint.py (run with assertions on, temp dir in scratch) gave 'Verified exact source patch replay: 16 files'. Every before-hash matched the baseline, every after-hash matched, and the patch applied with --fuzz=0. Its receipt files and 8 dependency hashes all matched.
binding.baseline: The baseline is the 717da106 deployed build source (commit e0fe3a00). The same baseline was used for the chonk-ipc review.

standalone_profile.construction: Shell::new_standalone_darwin uses SessionState::standalone_darwin(): a fixed NeXTSTEP Classic theme, Dark, scale 1.0, click-to-focus, autoreload disabled, no restore/omarchy/autostart/commands/terminal/session_env/monitor rules, and an evdev/pc105/us keymap at 25/500. The only bindings are Super+Return (SpawnTerminal) and Super+q (Close). In new_profile with standalone=true: no app scan or Rescanner thread; Desktop::new_standalone with an empty index and the built-in GraphiteFold wallpaper (no file load); no Omarchy menu; no ControlSocket; restore forced off; SessionLayout::start_at(None, ...) with no relaunch; autostart skipped. The Omarchy shell decision, appearance::publish and publish_button_layout (a background spawn thread in the generic profile) are all inside 'if !standalone'. There is no appearance RequestPoller, Omarchy Watch or Hyprland watch.
standalone_profile.initialization_pass: initialize_window_manager calls apply_session_state_inner with self.state.clone(). The inner function returns before appearance::publish/propagate_to_applications when scale, theme and style are unchanged (shell.rs ~1592-1608). It reloads the Omarchy menu only when reload_menu is set (false here) and follows the wallpaper only on a theme-id change. So the initialization pass reaches no external publisher. The CpuBackend accepts only the exact standalone keyboard configuration and otherwise records input_fault.
standalone_profile.runtime_paths: Standalone tick returns after the escape-dismiss and menu housekeeping, skipping miniwindows, layout persistence, appearance/Omarchy/rescan and control. run_action, run_menu_action and run_root_menu_action each return early for a managed Shell: Terminal goes to a ManagedBridge request; Close and End Session are handled; everything else is refused with a recorded reason. on_shell_click reaches side effects only through click_menu, then run_menu_action (gated). The standalone root menu offers only Terminal, End Session and a refusal row with action u32::MAX, which matches no command. The window menu offers only Close. on_notification's layout.claim has no recorded entries, and its persistence (service/flush) sits only in the skipped tick and shut_down paths. apply_session_state, resolve_live_config and set_appearance refuse in standalone. shut_down only begins the managed shutdown.
standalone_profile.audit_method_and_limit: I counted side-effect sinks per chonk-shell file (Command/spawn/thread/fs write/env/socket) and traced every Shell entry point that DesktopSession calls (constructor, initialize_window_manager, apply_workareas, keymap_action/keymap_release_action, run_action, run_menu_key, on_shell_click, on_root_press, on_motion, on_notification, tick, cancel_transient_menus, begin_managed_shutdown, complete_managed_request). Every generic spawn_* or launch_* call site found sits behind the managed early return or a !standalone guard. This is a targeted source trace, not a whole-program call-graph proof of Desktop and wm-core internals. That matches the checkpoint's own admission_remaining item.

input_ownership_and_popup.keys: The Shell sees every key first (input.rs desktop_key). A consumed press is added to suppressed_keys and sets deferred_focus. A consumed release retires the forwarded key. While keyboard_grabbed, unconsumed keys go only to wm-core and are intercepted from clients. sync_input_focus withholds client keyboard focus while grabbed or deferred, and until pressed_keys is empty, so a client gets wl_keyboard.leave during menus and Alt+Tab and re-enters with no held keys. That matches frozen app DS1/DS5. While a menu is visible, keymap_action consumes every press (arrows/Enter/Space map to menu keys; Escape is parked for tick; modifier combos are consumed), so Alt+Tab cannot start a wm-core cycle under an open menu.
input_ownership_and_popup.pointer: desktop_pointer runs only with no forwarded client buttons and no WM drag. A popup is modal: clicks outside shell surfaces cancel menus and are consumed. Client and frame hits go to the WM when no popup is open. Pointer input is consumed while wm-core's Alt+Tab cycle holds the keyboard. A consumed event sends a pointer motion with no focus, so the client gets leave.
input_ownership_and_popup.popup_host: The CpuBackend PopupHost refuses create_popup during a WM drag. paint_popup validates size and length, or records input_fault. Shell motion and click queues are bounded at 256 each, or record input_fault, and are purged on surface destroy. Pointer and keyboard grabs are single-owner, enforced by assertions. Automatic and gesture menu opens check popup_can_open (no WM drag, no popup, no keyboard grab).
input_ownership_and_popup.host_evidence: The recorded logs show 29 library tests, 4 real-Wayland tests (including shared_shell_modal_launch_chord_does_not_enter_new_client_as_text_or_release) and 2 managed-bridge tests passing. Strict clippy fails only on the 2 declared baseline lints (preserved as a failure). I did not rerun cargo, to avoid writing build output into the source tree.

notes.N1_assertion_panics_need_entry_handling: Grab and drag ownership conflicts in CpuBackend are assertions, which panic. The paths I examined guard against nesting, but a panic would bypass the manager's owned cleanup (the library has no Drop reaper, by design). The future native entry (002) needs an explicit panic strategy that still drives or records owned-application shutdown. The frozen app separately cleans up its own PTY on Wayland disconnect.
notes.N2_default_wm_binding: wm.bind_default_keys() keeps wm-core's Alt+Tab / Alt+Shift+Tab switcher in standalone (an in-WM keyboard grab with no external effect). The profile description lists only Super+Return and Super+q, so this binding should be documented as part of the standalone profile.
notes.N3_unprompted_refusal_menu: A refused managed launch automatically reopens the root menu at the pointer to show the refusal. It is gated by popup_can_open and follows only a user request, but it takes a modal grab, so the focused client gets leave. This is acceptable and consistent with DS1.
notes.N4_pointer_swallow_on_grab: Pointer input is consumed whenever keyboard_grabbed is set without a popup. That is intended for the Alt+Tab cycle, but a leaked grab would freeze pointer input. The assertion pairing makes a leak a panic rather than a silent stall, which leads back to N1.

cross_boundary_observations.X1_kill_orphans_app_pty_session: The manager signals only the app PID (TERM, then KILL after 5 s). The frozen app puts its shell in a separate session, and the protocol does not carry the shell PID. So a KILL path (a hung app) can leave the app's shell and its descendants running until reboot. A missing or incomplete CLEANUP is already a failure; runtime qualification should record a KILL as possibly having orphaned the shell. The app's normal post-TERM cleanup (about 0.25 + 2 + 0.25 s plus fsync) fits inside the 5 s grace.
cross_boundary_observations.X2_deadline_race: The manager's application_deadline is lifetime N counted from Lifecycle::new, before spawn. The app counts the same N from its own start, so the manager's TERM normally arrives just before the app's own deadline. The app's stop_cause then reads 'signal' rather than 'deadline'. Both are normal stops by contract, so this only affects diagnostics; a small manager grace beyond N would let the app's own deadline stop be observed. The READY bounds are compatible (app 20 s, manager 25 s).
cross_boundary_observations.X3_socket_path_bound: TerminalLauncher accepts socket paths up to 900 bytes, while the app refuses anything over 103 bytes. That fails closed at app start but could be checked before spawning.
